sentences: Let's call this session to order and confirm we have quorum before working through tonight's agenda.
The clerk will take the roll, and I'd ask members to hold amendments until public comment closes.
I move we adopt the agenda as printed, with one amendment moving item six ahead of item four.
Once the roll is confirmed, we'll proceed in order and I intend to adjourn by nine sharp.
Turning to zoning, the proposed overlay would let two more housing units rise on these parcels.
Several landlords have written in about the new permit fees, and I think their concerns deserve a hearing.
Our vacancy rate downtown has fallen below three percent, which tells me density near transit corridors has to increase.
I'd like the planning office to fast-track permits for accessory units, since that's the fastest lever we have on supply.
Patrol staffing in the east precinct remains thin, and residents keep asking why response times have slipped this quarter.
Moving to the budget, the mid-year appropriation request from public works exceeds what our reserve fund can comfortably absorb.
I want an independent audit of the parks fund before we approve any new levy on the November ballot.
Staff project a modest deficit next fiscal year unless we trim discretionary spending across every department.
The new light-rail station at Fifth and Main is nearly finished, and I'm eager to see ridership along that corridor grow.
Riders have complained that the transfer window between the bus route and the rail line is too tight to make.
I'd support revising the timetable so the last departure from the depot lines up with second-shift workers getting off.
Before we go further, I'll note we're short a member for a formal vote, so let's confirm quorum again.
Back to public safety, I've asked the chief to explain why dispatch hold times have climbed since spring.
Officers walking a beat downtown say foot patrols build more trust than cruisers ever could.
I remain uneasy about how warrant requests are being logged and want that process reviewed by the oversight board.
The precinct's overtime budget is ballooning, and I'd rather see that money go toward hiring than backfilling shifts.
Shifting to conservation, the watershed study flagged three sites where sediment is choking the stream year after year.
Restoring the wetland buffer along the creek would do more for flood control than any storm drain we could build.
One more transit item before we close: the depot expansion still needs a construction easement from the county.
Finally, replacing the parking lot behind city hall with tree canopy would cut runoff and improve air quality near the particulate monitors.
I'll bring the meeting to order and ask the clerk to confirm we have quorum on the dais tonight.
Please note the amendment to tonight's agenda moving the housing item up ahead of the consent calendar.
Let's take the roll before we open the floor to any further amendments from the council.
Barring objection, I intend to gavel this session closed no later than nine-thirty and adjourn promptly.
The rezoning application before us would raise density along the corridor while easing our permit backlog.
Tenants have told me their landlord raised rent the same week the vacancy notice went up next door.
I support streamlining the permit process for accessory dwelling units so more small housing gets built faster.
Current zoning caps block exactly the kind of infill housing this neighborhood has been asking for.
On the budget, the proposed appropriation for street repaving is reasonable given how thin our reserve has gotten.
I'd like a fiscal note attached before we vote, since last year's audit flagged weak tracking on capital projects.
Raising the levy even slightly would close most of the projected deficit without touching core services.
Finance should walk us through the reserve balance again, because the numbers in this appropriation packet don't match last month's.
The new transit hub near the station has already cut average commute times for residents on that side of town.
I've heard complaints that the transfer point downtown leaves riders standing in the rain for twenty minutes.
Before we leave infrastructure, the watershed report on stormwater capacity near the rail yard deserves a closer look.
I'd like the timetable adjusted so evening buses actually meet the last train out of the depot.
Turning to public safety, dispatch response in the north precinct has improved since the new software rolled out.
I still want clarity on how patrol officers are deciding which calls get priority after midnight.
Residents on Elm Street say they haven't seen an officer walk the beat there in months.
Any warrant executed in a residential area should be logged and reported to this council within a week.
Returning briefly to finance, I'd rather delay the audit than rush it and miss real fiscal problems.
The wetland restoration near the reservoir is finally showing results, with runoff levels down noticeably this spring.
One last housing note: the vacancy figures citywide still don't reflect what's happening in the units above Main Street.
I'll close by asking staff to study whether expanding the tree canopy could offset the particulate levels near the depot.
